exclusion_rationale.summary: Corll was shot dead on 8 August 1973 by Elmer Wayne Henley Jr., one of the two accomplices who then led police to the burial sites. He was never arrested, never charged and never tried. The evidentiary basis against him is unusually strong for an unadjudicated case — two co-offenders were convicted of murders committed with him, and the appellate opinions in their cases describe his conduct in detail — but no court has ever tested a case against Corll himself, and this dataset does not convict people posthumously. He is recorded here rather than on the offender roster for that reason alone.

judicial_findings.value: Two men were convicted of murders committed with Corll, and the published opinions in their appeals describe his role. Elmer Wayne Henley Jr. was convicted on six counts of murder with malice in the 175th District Court, Bexar County, and sentenced to 99 years on each count, consecutively (affirmed 1978). David Owen Brooks was convicted of murder with malice and sentenced to life (affirmed 1979). The Henley opinion records that the victims were restrained at Corll's house, sexually assaulted and tortured before being shot or strangled, and that the bodies were transported in a wooden box to three burial sites outside Houston.

judicial_findings.notes: These are findings against Henley and Brooks. They are the strongest material in the record about Corll's conduct, and they are still not findings against Corll: he had no counsel, made no defence, and cross-examined nobody. The distinction is the reason this is a case record.

physical_evidence.value: Twenty-seven bodies were recovered following Henley's disclosures, from three sites: a boat shed in south-west Houston, the Lake Sam Rayburn area, and High Island beach. Eight were found at the boat shed in the first phase of digging.

cause_of_death_determination.notes: Per-victim autopsy findings have not been retrieved. The appellate opinions state that victims were shot or strangled, but that is a summary of the confession evidence rather than a report of medical-examiner determinations, and this dataset does not treat the two as equivalent. homicide_attribution.value: No homicide is judicially attributed to Corll. The twenty-seven recoveries are attributed to the series in which Henley and Brooks were convicted; the convictions establish their participation, not a court's allocation of any death to Corll personally.

victim_count_claims.value: Three figures circulate. Twenty-seven — the number of bodies recovered, stated in the 1978 appellate opinion. Twenty-eight — the number of sets of remains now counted by Houston media, of which twenty-seven have been identified and one, known as John Doe 1973, has not. Twenty-nine and higher — used in later feature coverage without a stated basis. Brooks's own confession gave 'between 25 and thirty boys'. None of these is recorded as a victim count for Corll.

research_value.why_recorded: Corll is the clearest test of the roster/case boundary in the dataset. Unlike Larry Hall, where the question is whether the offences happened at all, here two co-offenders were convicted and the appellate record describes the conduct in detail. The evidentiary basis is strong and the exclusion is still correct, because the criterion is adjudication and no court ever adjudicated him. Recording him this way makes the rule visible: the dataset excludes on procedure, not on doubt. The case is also the dataset's limit case for detection — no agency identified the series, and it ended when one participant shot the other and telephoned police.
